title: dev 部署 release-artifacts 保留期限＋build cache 上限＋磁碟預檢
summary: Implements pre-build release-artifact retention in scripts/dev_release_artifact_retention.py deriving kept sets strictly from existing manifests and never deleting the image tars of the currently served release (including across FE-only deploys or baseline-only captures); protects every running or stopped compose container image with pantheon-protect/<service>:<id12> before docker builder prune -f --keep-storage 20GB (forbidding builder prune -a/-af, removing stale protect tags only for unused images, and skipping builder prune with a logged reason if any container image cannot be protected); keeps unused-image prune opt-in behind PANTHEON_DEV_DOCKER_PRUNE=true; enforces a 25GB free-disk preflight floor before the dev root build; and documents the policy in docs/deployment/vm-dev-staging-prod-management-plan.md.

acceptance_verification.description: Before the dev root build and while holding the dev environment lease, the deploy applies a retention policy to pantheon-ci-deploy/release-artifacts: it keeps every image archive, compose bundle, and baseline folder referenced by the currently served release, the last 3 accepted releases, the in-flight candidate, and the latest captured rollback baseline; all other entries are deleted and the deleted count and bytes are logged.

Retention never deletes a file referenced by any kept manifest even when archives are shared between releases, and never deletes the release-artifacts image tars of the currently served release; tests build fixture roots proving shared and currently served archives survive and dry-run mode deletes nothing.

Docker build cache is bounded by default only with docker builder prune -f --keep-storage (default 20GB, never -a/-af) after enumerating every compose container (running or stopped) and protecting its image with pantheon-protect/<service>:<id12> (removing stale protect tags only for images no container uses, or skipping the prune with a logged reason if any container image cannot be protected); a test proves a container's untagged image survives the cache bound while unused-image prune stays opt-in behind PANTHEON_DEV_DOCKER_PRUNE.

After retention and the cache bound, a disk preflight fails the deploy before any build with an explicit insufficient-disk message when free space on the deploy filesystem is below a configurable floor (default 25GB).

docs/deployment/vm-dev-staging-prod-management-plan.md documents the retention rule, container image protection and cache bound, and the disk floor; existing release-artifact and restore tests stay green.
